title: Obsidian
subtitle: Black that commands light rather than borrowing it.

stone.origin: Black has its own authority. It does not borrow light. It commands it. Stone to stone in white gold — a continuous line, unbroken from start to finish.

metal: white gold — a continuous line, unbroken from start to finis
description: Black has its own authority — it does not borrow light, it commands it. Obsidian runs black diamonds stone to stone in white gold, a single continuous line unbroken from clasp to clasp, so the darkness reads as one deliberate surface around the wrist. Against the bright metal the stones hold their depth, absorbing light at the centre and returning only a hard edge of it at the facets. There is no colour here to soften the statement and none is wanted. It is restraint worn as strength.
